title: Best AthenaHQ Alternatives (2026): Free, Instant Picks Compared
metaDescription: Looking for AthenaHQ alternatives in 2026? Compare AEOeye, Otterly, Peec, and Profound on price, free tiers, AI engines, and best-fit use case.
shortAnswer: The best AthenaHQ alternative depends on how you want to start. If you want a free, instant look at your AI visibility with no card and no sales call, AEOeye is the fastest on-ramp. Otterly ($29/mo, 14-day trial) and Peec ($89/mo, unlimited seats) are strong low-cost trackers, while Profound competes with AthenaHQ at the enterprise tier.
intro:
AthenaHQ is a capable GEO (generative engine optimization) platform: it tracks how your brand shows up across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot and more, with sentiment, competitor benchmarking, citation tracking, and an action center for fixes. It's a serious tool. The friction is getting in the door — there's no free tier and no true trial, the cheapest plan is $295/month, and several of the features people want most live behind a custom Enterprise contract.

If you're here, you probably want to see your AI visibility *before* committing $295. Below we cover, factually, why people look past AthenaHQ — then walk through real alternatives, starting with AEOeye (free and instant) and including Otterly, Peec, and Profound described fairly, with a side-by-side table.

sections.heading: Why people look for AthenaHQ alternatives: the $295 entry price
sections.body:
The most common reason is simple: there's no way to try AthenaHQ for free. No free tier, no true free trial. The cheapest route in is the Self-Serve plan at $295/month (about $245/month if you pay annually), softened only by a roughly 67% discount on the first month — around $97 — that still requires upfront payment.

Reviewers repeatedly flag this as a steep commitment just to evaluate the tool. For a solopreneur, a small in-house team, or anyone who only wants a quick read on whether AI engines mention their brand, paying ~$97–$295 before seeing a single result is a real barrier. It's not that AthenaHQ is overpriced for what it does — it's that the on-ramp assumes you've already decided to buy. That assumption is exactly what pushes people to look for something they can run first, then upgrade from if it proves worthwhile.

sections.heading: Why people look elsewhere: unpredictable credit-based pricing
sections.body:
AthenaHQ's pricing is usage-based. Roughly speaking, one credit equals one tracked AI response, and the Self-Serve plan includes 3,600 credits per month. That sounds generous until you do the math on real monitoring: tracking many prompts, across multiple engines, refreshed regularly, burns credits quickly.

Teams report running out mid-month and buying overages — sold in blocks of about 1,250 credits (~$100, or roughly $0.08/credit). The result is that your actual monthly bill can drift well above the advertised $295, and it's hard to forecast in advance because it depends on how aggressively you monitor. For budgeting, that unpredictability is a genuine drawback. Several alternatives use flat prompt-based plans instead (you know exactly what you get for the price), which some teams find easier to plan around even if the headline number looks similar.

sections.heading: Why people look elsewhere: best features locked behind Enterprise
sections.body:
A lot of what makes AthenaHQ exciting in a demo turns out to be Enterprise-only. The Citation/ACE engine, multi-region and persona targeting, API access, BI-tool integrations (Tableau/Looker), SSO, and the more advanced content-optimization tooling all sit on the custom Enterprise tier — generally quoted from around $2,000+/month.

The Self-Serve plan, meanwhile, is limited to a single country and more basic tooling. So several reviewers describe coming in at $295, then discovering that the specific capability they signed up for — multi-market tracking, citations, integrations — requires a custom Enterprise contract almost immediately. That's a reasonable structure for a platform aimed at large brands, but it means Self-Serve can feel like a stepping stone rather than a destination. If you need those features and don't have an enterprise budget, it's worth comparing tools that include more in their mid-tier plans.

sections.heading: AEOeye — free, instant, multi-engine (start here)
sections.body:
AEOeye is the fastest way to answer the question that sends people to AthenaHQ in the first place: *do AI engines actually recommend my brand?* It's free to start and instant — no credit card, no sales call, no contract. You enter your brand and it asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini the questions real buyers ask, then shows whether each engine recommends you, where you rank, and which competitors are winning the answer.

The approach is blind multi-engine querying across all five major engines at once, which makes it genuinely useful for non-experts who just want a clear read rather than a dashboard to configure. It's the natural first step before paying for ongoing monitoring anywhere.

Honest limits: AEOeye is newer and lighter on enterprise analytics and long-horizon historical dashboards than incumbents like AthenaHQ or Profound. Its deeper multi-engine querying activates with usage rather than arriving as a heavy enterprise suite on day one. If you need multi-region tracking, BI integrations and SSO today, an enterprise platform fits better. If you want an honest, immediate look — and a low-friction way to keep watching — start here, free.

sections.heading: Otterly, Peec, and Profound — fair picks for different needs
sections.body:
**Otterly** is the lowest-cost ongoing tracker here. Plans start at $29/month (Lite, ~15 prompts), with a 14-day free trial and no card required. It reruns your prompts daily across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Copilot, storing history into a brand-visibility index with citation and share-of-voice reports. Note that Gemini and Google AI Mode are paid add-ons. It earned Gartner Cool Vendor 2025 recognition. Great for small teams wanting affordable, scheduled monitoring.

**Peec** starts at $89/month (Starter: ~25 prompts, 3 countries) and is popular with agencies and B2B SaaS teams. Its standout is unlimited seats on every plan — no per-head tax — plus clean competitor benchmarking. Base plans cover three engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews); Claude, Gemini, Copilot and others are ~€20–30/engine add-ons, so budget for the engines you need.

**Profound** is the closest enterprise peer to AthenaHQ. It offers deep analytics, prompt-volume data, and strong share-of-voice and sentiment work — but it has moved to an enterprise-only, sales-led model with custom pricing (generally $2,000+/month) and no self-serve trial. Best when you're running a large, well-resourced GEO program.

keyTakeaways: AthenaHQ has no free tier and no true trial — entry is $295/month (about $97 for a discounted first month), which prices out smaller teams that just want a look.
Pricing is credit-based (3,600/month, ~$0.08/credit overages), so heavy multi-engine monitoring can push real cost well above the sticker price.
Top features — ACE Citation Engine, multi-region, API, BI integrations, SSO — are Enterprise-only (~$2,000+/mo); Self-Serve is single-country.
AEOeye is the best free, instant alternative: blind multi-engine querying across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini with no card and no sales call.
Otterly ($29/mo, 14-day trial) and Peec ($89/mo, unlimited seats) are strong low-cost ongoing trackers; Profound competes with AthenaHQ at the enterprise tier.
Match the tool to your stage: free audit to start (AEOeye), affordable monitoring next (Otterly/Peec), enterprise analytics later (AthenaHQ/Profound).

faqs.q: Does AthenaHQ have a free trial?
faqs.a: No. AthenaHQ has no free tier and no true free trial. The cheapest way in is the Self-Serve plan at $295/month, softened by a roughly 67% first-month discount (around $97) that still requires upfront payment. If you only want to see whether AI engines recommend your brand, a free instant audit like AEOeye lets you check before paying anything.

faqs.q: What's the cheapest alternative to AthenaHQ?
faqs.a: AEOeye is free to start — you can run an instant AI visibility audit with no credit card. Among paid trackers, Otterly is the lowest entry point at $29/month (with a 14-day free trial), and Peec starts at $89/month with unlimited seats. Profound, by contrast, has moved to enterprise-only custom pricing, so it's not a budget option.

faqs.q: How is AEOeye different from AthenaHQ?
faqs.a: AEOeye is built to be free and instant: it asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini the questions real buyers ask, then shows whether they recommend you, where you rank, and which competitors win — no contract, no sales call. AthenaHQ is a heavier, paid platform with deeper enterprise analytics and historical dashboards. AEOeye is newer and lighter on those enterprise features; its deeper multi-engine querying activates with ongoing usage.

faqs.q: Will switching to a cheaper tool give me worse data?
faqs.a: Not necessarily for the core job. Tracking brand mentions, rank, sentiment, citations and competitors across major AI engines is something tools like AEOeye, Otterly and Peec all do well. AthenaHQ and Profound add depth — prompt-volume data, multi-region, citation engines, BI integrations — that matters for large programs. Pick based on whether you need a quick honest read or enterprise-grade analytics.

faqs.q: Which AthenaHQ alternative is best for agencies?
faqs.a: Peec is a common agency pick because it includes unlimited seats on every plan, so clients and teammates don't add per-head cost. AEOeye is useful for agencies that want to run fast, free audits during pitches or onboarding. For enterprise clients needing multi-region tracking and API/BI access, AthenaHQ Enterprise or Profound are the heavier options.
